notes: Perfect claim overlap (C102, C103). Both agree that mitochondrial division differs mechanistically from bacterial division, with division sites positioned adjacent to nucleoids rather than excluded from them.

High claim overlap (C61-C68, 8/9 claims shared). LLM finds structure-function analysis strongly supports both GTPase domains being required for Gem1 function. Reviewers view evidence as incomplete and request additional rescue experiments for GTPase and calcium binding domain mutations.

High claim overlap (C8, C9, C44, C86, C88-C91, 8/10 claims shared). LLM finds strong support for spatial coupling of nucleoids to ERMD based on colocalization and segregation data. Reviewers question whether division and nucleoid segregation are obligatorily linked and request additional data on GEM1 deletion effects on nucleoid distribution.

Moderate claim overlap (C46, C47, C51, C52, 4/11 claims shared). LLM supports ERMES localization to division sites based on time-lapse imaging. Reviewers express concern that observed structures may represent post-division tethers rather than active division sites, requesting better visualization to distinguish these scenarios.

Partial claim overlap (C57-C60, C70, C71, 6/24 claims shared). LLM supports stable ERMES-associated constrictions in gem1Δ cells. Reviewers express difficulty distinguishing constriction sites from separate mitochondria with ER tubules between them, requesting clarification.

Partial claim overlap (C5, C6, C43, C84, C85, C115, 6/24 claims shared). Both agree on Gem1's role as negative regulator of ER-mitochondria contacts and its function in tip resolution. Reviewers accept the core regulatory function without challenging the fundamental claims.

Partial claim overlap (C77-C81, 5/24 claims shared). LLM supports increased ER-mitochondria contact surface area in gem1Δ based on EM quantification. Reviewers identify apparent discrepancy with Kornmann et al. 2011 regarding ERMES foci size/number, requesting clarification on whether some contacts lack ERMES complexes.

Minimal claim overlap (C4, C41, 2/11 claims shared). Both accept the fundamental spatial and functional linkage between ERMES, Gem1, and ERMD. Reviewers find the work rigorous and interesting without challenging core findings.

Minimal claim overlap (C42, 1/7 claims shared). LLM rates integrative model as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct mechanistic evidence. Reviewers accept the fundamental linkage as SUPPORTED, though both acknowledge mechanistic details need development.
Claims C55, C56, C123 regarding Gem1 colocalization with ERMES at division sites only evaluated by LLM. No corresponding peer review assessment found for these specific colocalization observations.

Claims C97-C101 regarding conservation of ERMD/Miro role in mammalian systems only evaluated by LLM as UNCERTAIN. No corresponding peer review assessment found for these evolutionary conservation claims.
